name: Form EIA-860 Annual Electric Generator Report
reveals: Generator-level inventory (nameplate MW, fuel, prime mover, owner, planned/retired units, lat/long) for every plant >=1 MW, including on-site and behind-the-meter gas turbines and proposed units that are increasingly tied to data-center campuses. Cross-match plant coordinates with data-center sites to attribute dedicated generation.
update_frequency: Annual final (Sept); early-release June; monthly generator inventory (EIA-860M)
scrape_hint: Download yearly ZIP of XLSX; join Plant/Generator sheets on Plant Code; EIA-860M monthly for proposed units; or EIA API v2 (free key at eia.gov/opendata) route electricity/operating-generator-capacity.

name: Form EIA-923 Power Plant Operations Report
reveals: Monthly fuel consumption and net generation per plant and prime mover, so fuel burned by gas plants serving data-center load growth (or on-site plants) can be quantified in MMBtu and MWh. Also includes cooling-water data schedules (8A-8F) for thermoelectric plants.
scrape_hint: ZIP of XLSX per year; Page 1 sheet has plant-level monthly fuel/generation; Schedule 8 for cooling water withdrawal/consumption.

name: Emissions & Generation Resource Integrated Database (eGRID)
reveals: Plant- and subregion-level emission rates (CO2, NOx, SO2 lb/MWh), generation and resource mix; the standard factor set for converting a site's metered or estimated MWh into location-based emissions independent of company market-based claims.
scrape_hint: Download eGRID XLSX from the Detailed Data page; PLNT sheet keyed on ORISPL (same as EIA plant code); GIS shapefiles of subregions available on Maps page.

name: Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) facility data / FLIGHT
reveals: Facility-level reported GHG emissions (~8,000 facilities >25,000 tCO2e) including stationary combustion; a data-center campus whose on-site generators or gas turbines cross the threshold appears here under its own name or an LLC, revealing real fuel burn.
update_frequency: Annual, released each October (RY2025 deadline extended to March 2027; program scope under proposed rollback)
scrape_hint: Use FLIGHT export (XLS) filtered by NAICS 518210 or by state; or Envirofacts GHG REST API (https://enviro.epa.gov/enviro/efservice/...) for CSV/JSON.

name: FERC eLibrary
reveals: Full text of filings: large-load interconnection agreements, co-location/behind-the-meter disputes (e.g., nuclear-plant co-location dockets), transmission service requests and utility Form 1/EQR data. Dockets name the specific sites, MW and fuel behind data-center load.
scrape_hint: Use the docket-number or full-text search with terms like 'data center' + 'interconnection'; results can be bulk-zipped; no official API, but the search UI posts JSON to an internal endpoint that can be replayed.

name: PJM Serial/Cycle Service Request Status (interconnection queue) and Data Miner 2 API
country_or_scope: United States (13 states + DC; incl. Northern Virginia)
reveals: Queue of generation and transmission service requests with MW, fuel and location; combined with PJM load forecasts identifies the gas and battery projects being attached to data-center load growth in Dominion/Loudoun. Data Miner 2 provides hourly load by zone.
update_frequency: Queue XLSX updated as cycles progress; Data Miner feeds hourly/daily
scrape_hint: Download queue Excel from the status pages; for Data Miner 2 register a PJM Tools account, request free API key (non-commercial), then GET https://api.pjm.com/api/v1/... with Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header; gridstatus library wraps both.

name: ERCOT Large Load Interconnection queue status updates
reveals: ERCOT reported ~410 GW of large-load requests as of March 2026, ~87.6% data centers, and 9,456 MW approved to energize (July 2026 Monthly Operational Overview). Stage-by-stage counts (no studies, under review, approved, energized) are the only non-company view of Texas AI load.
update_frequency: Monthly (Monthly Operational Overview) plus board/TAC presentations; a Large Load Portal is in development
scrape_hint: Scrape ercot.com/files/docs/ listings for 'LLI Queue Status Update' and 'Monthly Operational Overview' PDFs; parse tables with pdfplumber; county-level MW appears in TAC/Board decks. Landing pages: ercot.com/gridinfo/load and ercot.com/services/rq/large-load (JS-rendered).

name: MISO Generator Interconnection Queue (interactive map + JSON endpoint)
reveals: All active/withdrawn generation requests with fuel, MW, county, POI and study status; map refreshes every 30 minutes. Used to see what gas capacity is queuing near announced data-center sites (e.g., Louisiana, Indiana, Ohio-adjacent).
scrape_hint: GET https://www.misoenergy.org/api/giqueue/getprojects returns JSON of the full queue (as used by the gridstatus library).

name: SPP Generator Interconnection active queue (OPS Portal)
reveals: Active GI requests with MW, fuel, county and study cluster, plus Power BI dashboards of queue and commercial-operation dates; relevant for Oklahoma/Kansas/Texas-panhandle data-center build-outs.
update_frequency: Weekly status PDF; queue page continuous
scrape_hint: GET https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateSummaryCSV for a CSV of the active queue; HTML view at opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive.

name: NYISO Interconnection Queue
reveals: Generation, transmission and load interconnection requests (NYISO explicitly covers 'load facilities'), with MW, fuel, county and study status; the load-side entries are a direct signal of large data-center sites.
scrape_hint: Direct XLSX: https://www.nyiso.com/documents/20142/1407078/NYISO-Interconnection-Queue.xlsx ; filter the Type column for load projects.

name: Queued Up: interconnection queue dataset (2026 edition, data through 2025)
country_or_scope: United States (7 ISOs + 50 non-ISO utilities, ~98% of capacity)
reveals: Cleaned, harmonised national interconnection-queue dataset (fuel, MW, county, status, dates) under CC BY 4.0; the fastest way to map which gas, storage and solar projects are queuing in data-center counties without parsing seven ISO formats.
scrape_hint: Download the ~15 MB XLSX from the page; one row per project; join to county FIPS.

name: Virginia State Corporation Commission Docket Search
reveals: Dominion Energy IRP, rate and CPCN cases (PUR- dockets) containing data-center load forecasts, large-load contracts, new gas-plant proposals and transmission lines serving Loudoun/Prince William; filings posted within 24-48 h.
scrape_hint: Docket Search portal at scc.virginia.gov/clk/docketsearch (robots.txt blocks crawlers; use browser automation); search 'data center' within PUR case types; PDFs are text-searchable.

name: Georgia PSC FACTS docket search
reveals: Georgia Power IRP and certification dockets with large-load (data-center) pipeline MW, proposed gas turbines and PPAs; searchable by docket, company, industry and date.
scrape_hint: Use the Search Document Filings form (industry=Electric, description contains 'data center'); result pages link directly to PDFs; no bulk export.

name: Public Utility Commission of Texas Interchange filings
reveals: Project dockets on large-load interconnection rules (e.g., SB6 implementation), CCN transmission cases serving data-center clusters, and utility load-growth filings; searchable by control number, utility, filing party and date.
scrape_hint: Search by control number (e.g., 56000-series large load rulemakings); each item has a stable download URL; no API.

name: Louisiana PSC Document Access Center
reveals: Entergy Louisiana dockets approving dedicated gas plants and contracts for hyperscale data-center load (e.g., Richland Parish), with testimony on MW, fuel and cost allocation; results exportable to Excel/PDF.
scrape_hint: Search dockets by company 'Entergy Louisiana' and keyword; export result list to Excel; large result sets must be narrowed by date (per LPSC access guide PDF).

name: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform
reveals: Hourly/15-min load, generation by fuel, unit-level generation (>100 MW), outages and cross-border flows per bidding zone; baseline for estimating marginal fuel for data-center load in Ireland, Netherlands, Nordics, Germany.
scrape_hint: Register, email transparency@entsoe.eu for 'RESTful API access' (granted in ~3 working days), generate token; use entsoe-py client; export also via UI as CSV/XML.

name: Data Centres Metered Electricity Consumption
reveals: Official metered share of national electricity used by data centres (5% in 2015, 21% in 2023, 22% in 2024), by quarter and region; the only national statistics office series derived from meter data rather than operator reporting.
scrape_hint: Tables are in PxStat; query the JSON-stat API at https://ws.cso.ie/public/api.restful/PxStat.Data.Cube_API.ReadDataset/<table>/JSON-stat/2.0/en.

name: EirGrid Data Centre Constrained Area Overview and heat maps
reveals: ~2 GW of contracted data-centre demand (mostly greater Dublin, fully constrained) and ~6 GW of further expressed interest; indicative 50-100 MW headroom at 220 kV sites in Galway/Limerick/Cork. EirGrid's annual Generation Capacity Statement gives contracted/connected data-centre MVA.
update_frequency: Ad hoc revisions (R1 May 2026); Generation Capacity Statement annual
scrape_hint: Pull PDFs from cms.eirgrid.ie/sites/default/files/publications/ ; parse the demand tables; FOI disclosure log lists additional data-centre connection records released.

name: Capaciteitskaart elektriciteitsnet (grid congestion map)
publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / TenneT and regional DSOs
reveals: Map of offtake (afname) and feed-in congestion per substation area with queue status (capacity available / partially / under investigation / shortage with waiting list); shows where data-center load can and cannot connect.
update_frequency: Continuous (map had a loading error at check time)
scrape_hint: Map is a JS app loading GeoJSON layers; capture the XHR layer URLs in browser devtools and fetch them directly; separate TenneT and regional views.

name: NESO Transmission Entry Capacity (TEC) Register and connection registers
reveals: Every project holding a transmission connection contract (MW, technology, connection site, date, Gate 1/2 status); the companion registers in the 'Connection registers' group include demand connections, which expose data-center sites and the generation queued alongside them.
scrape_hint: CKAN-style API: GET https://api.neso.energy/api/3/action/package_show?id=transmission-entry-capacity-tec-register then download CSV resource URL; NESO Open Data Licence.

name: Fingrid Open Data
reveals: Real-time and historical consumption, production by type, frequency and reserve data via REST API; baseline for Finnish data-center hubs (Hamina, Espoo, Kajaani) and for checking hourly-CFE claims.
scrape_hint: Sign up for API key; GET https://data.fingrid.fi/api/datasets/{id}/data?startTime=...&endTime=... with x-api-key header; CSV/JSON.

name: Energi Data Service
reveals: Consumption per municipality/industry code, production per fuel, CO2 intensity (5-min), district-heating-related datasets; lets a ledger localise data-center electricity (Fredericia, Odense, Viborg) and verify grid intensity.
scrape_hint: No key needed: GET https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/ConsumptionIndustry?limit=... returns JSON; CSV/XLSX export from UI.

name: AEMO NEM data (NEMWeb, MMS)
reveals: 5-minute dispatch, unit-level generation and scheduled load, regional demand, plus connections-scorecard and Generation Information lists of proposed plants; Sydney/Melbourne data-center load appears in regional demand forecasts (ESOO/IASR).
scrape_hint: Crawl https://nemweb.com.au/Reports/Current/ directory listings for zipped CSVs; NEMOSIS Python package automates; connections scorecard is a monthly XLSX/PDF.

name: EU data centre energy performance reporting (EED Art.12 / Delegated Reg. 2024/1364) - national guidance
publisher: European Commission database; Irish DCEE guidance page
reveals: Every data centre >=500 kW IT load must report annually (by 15 May) energy, PUE, water use, waste-heat reuse and renewable share to an EU database. As of this check the database is operator-login only (EU Login) and no public site-level extract has been released; the Commission is to publish aggregated results. Track for release.
scrape_hint: Nothing public to scrape yet; monitor energy.ec.europa.eu for the Commission's aggregated report and file access-to-documents requests (Reg. 1049/2001) for member-state aggregates.

name: Global Oil and Gas Plant Tracker
country_or_scope: Global (171 countries; units >=50 MW, >=20 MW in EU/UK)
reveals: 16,559 gas/oil units with status, owner, coordinates and 1,136 GW in development; the August 2026 release flags units proposed for data-center or captive supply, letting a ledger tie new fossil capacity to AI campuses worldwide.
scrape_hint: Request download via the form (email) to get the XLSX; summary tables are public Google Sheets; CC BY 4.0 attribution requested.

name: Global Coal Plant Tracker
reveals: 14,674 coal units with status, retirement dates and coordinates; used to document coal retirements deferred or cancelled to serve data-center load (US Midwest/South) and coal-backed grids hosting AI compute (China, India, Indonesia).
update_frequency: Twice yearly (Jan and Jul; latest July 2026)
scrape_hint: Download XLSX via the download page; join to GOGPT by owner; summary tables as Google Sheets.

name: CAISO Generator Interconnection public queue reports
reveals: Cluster 15/16 queue reports (XLSX) listing active, completed and withdrawn interconnection requests with MW, fuel and county; older clusters require RIMS login.
scrape_hint: Download the 'Cluster N Queue Report' XLSX links on the page; or gridstatus CAISO().get_interconnection_queue().

name: ISO-NE Interconnection Request Tracking Tool (public reports)
reveals: Tabular queue with request number, project name, fuel code, summer/winter MW, city/county/state, POI, transmission owner and in-service dates.
scrape_hint: Page renders a plain HTML table; parse with pandas.read_html.

name: EPA Enforcement and Compliance History Online (ECHO)
reveals: Facility-level Clean Air Act permit status, emissions inventories and inspections for >1.5 million regulated sites; querying NAICS 518210 or facility names surfaces data centers holding Title V/synthetic-minor permits for diesel generator fleets, whose permitted engine MW reveals true site capacity.
scrape_hint: ECHO Exporter ZIP for bulk; REST: https://echodata.epa.gov/echo/air_rest_services.get_facilities?p_naics=518210&output=JSON ; then DFR per registry ID.

name: Issued Air Permits for Data Centers (statewide list)
reveals: Dedicated page (launched Nov 2024) listing every data-center air permit in Virginia (177 at launch: 85 Loudoun, 34 Fairfax, 26 Prince William; Amazon 42, Microsoft 14) with PDF permits specifying number and kW rating of emergency generators and annual run-hour limits. Generator kW sum ~ site critical load.
scrape_hint: Page is a JS-rendered table (hash-bang route); confirmed via Virginia Mercury 2024-11-13 but direct fetch failed; load in headless browser, capture the JSON behind the table, then batch-download PDFs and regex 'kW' / 'generators'.

name: TCEQ Central Registry and Air Permit public notices
reveals: Regulated-entity records and air permits (PBR, standard permits, NSR) for Texas data centers; permit applications list engine counts and MW of diesel or gas generation, and public-notice pages give site addresses before construction.
scrape_hint: Query at https://www15.tceq.texas.gov/crpub/ (robots-blocked; form POST works from scripts) by name or SIC 7374/NAICS 518210; Central File Room online (records.tceq.texas.gov) holds permit PDFs.

name: Maricopa County Air Quality Public Records Viewer
reveals: ArcGIS map of permitted facilities with linked permit documents and public notices for the Phoenix/Goodyear/Mesa data-center corridor; permits list generator units and emissions caps.
scrape_hint: ArcGIS Web App; query the underlying FeatureServer REST endpoint (find via devtools) with where=1=1&outFields=*&f=json; public notices at maricopa.gov/1624/Public-Notices.

name: Environment Agency Public Registers Online
reveals: Installations register of environmental permits (incl. Medium Combustion Plant / Specified Generator permits that UK data centers need for >1 MW backup generators), water discharge and abstraction-related permits, searchable by operator or address with an API reference.
scrape_hint: Linked-data API: https://environment.data.gov.uk/public-register/installations/registration.json?_limit=... ; search 'data centre' in site name; permit PDFs linked.

name: EPA Ireland licence search and LEAP Online
reveals: Industrial Emissions (IED) licences for large data-centre campuses whose combined generator/gas-engine capacity exceeds 50 MW thermal (several Dublin campuses hold IED licences), with licence conditions, emissions limits and compliance records on LEAP.
scrape_hint: Search at epa.ie/our-services/licensing/licencesearch/ by applicant or class 2.1 (combustion); compliance and monitoring records at leap.epa.ie; application files are large PDFs.

name: Officiële bekendmakingen (Dutch official notices incl. permits)
reveals: All municipal/provincial gazette notices (~2,400/day) including omgevingsvergunning applications and decisions for datacenters (Haarlemmermeer, Middenmeer, Eemshaven, Zeewolde), noting generator installations and water use.
scrape_hint: Use the SRU API at https://repository.overheid.nl/sru?query=... (or zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/sru) with query 'datacenter' and publication type 'Gemeenteblad'; results in XML with PDF links.

name: European Industrial Emissions Portal (E-PRTR / IED)
reveals: Facility-level pollutant releases, waste transfers and large-combustion-plant energy input; IED-licensed data-centre campuses (e.g., Dublin) appear with reported NOx/CO2 and fuel input, an independent check on backup-generator run hours.
scrape_hint: Download full database (CSV/Access) from the portal's data page; filter by activity '1(c) combustion' or NACE 63.11.

name: USGS Estimated Use of Water in the United States (county-level)
reveals: County withdrawals by category (public supply, industrial, thermoelectric) every five years (2015 is the latest full county release; CC0); baseline against which data-center water demand in Loudoun, Maricopa, Umatilla etc. can be scaled.
update_frequency: Every 5 years (2015 latest county dataset; newer model-based estimates in progress)
scrape_hint: Download via DOI 10.5066/F7TB15V5 (XLSX/CSV); join on county FIPS.

name: Arizona Department of Water Resources data (Well Registry, AMA annual water use reports, GIS)
reveals: Well registry (Wells 55), grandfathered rights, groundwater levels and Active Management Area annual water-use reports by right holder; data centers in Phoenix AMA appear as industrial users or via municipal provider reports.
scrape_hint: GIS Data Center offers shapefiles/ArcGIS REST; AMA annual reports via 'Live Queries and Reports'; well data via Wells 55 map FeatureServer.

name: TWDB Water Use Survey and historical water use estimates
reveals: Mandatory annual survey of municipal, industrial, power and mining water users (Water Code 16.012m); published historical estimates by county/category and entity-level summaries expose large industrial users and the utilities supplying data centers.
scrape_hint: Use 'Historical Water Use Estimates' and 'Water Use Summary & Dashboards' pages (CSV/XLSX); entity-level survey responses via Public Information Act request.

name: Oregon Water Rights Information Query (WRIS)
reveals: Water right permits, certificates and transfers searchable by company name, basin and use type; data centers (The Dalles, Hillsboro, Prineville) hold or lease rights visible here, and transfers reveal new sources.
scrape_hint: Search by Name (company) with type of use 'Industrial/Commercial'; OWRD also publishes POD/POU GIS shapefiles on its GIS data page.

name: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 Water Risk Atlas
reveals: Baseline water stress and future projections per hydrological sub-basin (CC BY 4.0); lets a ledger classify each data-center site's basin stress and flag cooling-water draw in high-stress regions.
update_frequency: Major versions every few years (4.0 current)
scrape_hint: Download GDB/CSV from the Aqueduct data download page; point-in-polygon join on site coordinates.

name: Dirección General de Aguas - Catastro Público de Aguas and MEE
reveals: Public water-rights cadastre (derechos de aprovechamiento) and Monitoreo de Extracciones Efectivas (metered extractions by right holder); data centers in Santiago (Quilicura, Cerrillos) must hold or buy rights that appear here.
scrape_hint: CPA search portal is form-based (snia.mop.gob.cl/sad/ returned server error at check); query by titular name; MEE data available as downloadable reports.

name: Loudoun County LandMARC (land management and permits)
country_or_scope: United States (Loudoun County, VA - Data Center Alley)
reveals: Public records for site plans, building permits, zoning and grading applications; data-center site plans list building square footage, generator yards and substation locations, giving a build-stage inventory for the world's densest cluster.
scrape_hint: LandMARC is an Accela-style portal; search Plans by application type 'Site Plan' and keyword 'data center'; attachments are PDF; county also publishes a data-center GIS layer via its open data hub.

name: An Coimisiún Pleanála (formerly An Bord Pleanála) Case Search
reveals: Appeals and Strategic Infrastructure decisions on data-centre planning applications (Dublin, Ennis, Clonee), with inspector reports stating MW, generator counts, gas-plant proposals and water demand; map search and 1995-2015 archive.
scrape_hint: Case Search at pleanala.ie/en-ie/case-search supports keyword 'data centre'; inspector reports are PDFs; local-authority first-instance files on each council's planning portal.

name: SEIA e-SEIA (Sistema de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental)
reveals: Full environmental assessment files (DIA/EIA) for data-center projects, which must state MW, generator fleet, fuel storage and water consumption (e.g., Google Cerrillos, Microsoft, AWS projects); robots.txt blocked automated verification.
scrape_hint: Project search at seia.sea.gob.cl/busqueda/buscarProyecto.php; filter tipo de proyecto and keyword 'data center' / 'centro de datos'; expediente documents are PDFs.

name: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (Sentinel-1/2/3)
reveals: Free Sentinel-2 (10 m, ~5-day revisit) time series to confirm site clearing, building footprints, generator yards and substation construction; Sentinel-3 SLSTR thermal (1 km) and Sentinel-1 SAR for all-weather change detection.
scrape_hint: STAC: https://catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/stac ; OData/S3 download with free account token; openEO or Sentinel Hub for cloud processing within monthly free quota.

name: USGS EarthExplorer (Landsat 8/9 incl. TIRS thermal)
reveals: Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature (100 m thermal, 16-day/8-day with two satellites) to detect heat plumes and operating status of campuses; 30 m optical for expansion since 1980s.
scrape_hint: Create free EROS account; for scripting use the M2M API (https://m2m.cr.usgs.gov/, request access on profile): POST login-token, scene-search with bbox and datasetName 'landsat_ot_c2_l2', then download URLs; UI exports CSV/Shapefile.

name: Google Earth Engine
reveals: Cloud platform with Sentinel, Landsat, MODIS, night-lights (VIIRS) and the Satellite Embedding dataset; free for academic/research/non-profit use; allows per-site NDBI/LST time series and night-light growth over hundreds of campuses in minutes.
scrape_hint: Register a non-commercial Cloud project; use Python 'ee' API: ee.ImageCollection('LANDSAT/LC09/C02/T1_L2') filterBounds(site).select('ST_B10').

name: OpenStreetMap telecom=data_center features (via Overpass API)
reveals: Crowd-mapped data-center buildings/campuses with operator, name, building footprints and lifecycle tags (proposed:/construction:); a free global seed list of site polygons to drive satellite and permit lookups.
scrape_hint: Overpass QL: [out:json]; (nwr["telecom"="data_center"]; nwr["building"="data_center"]; nwr["industrial"="data_centre"];); out center tags; via https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter.

name: NASA ECOSTRESS (ISS thermal radiometer)
reveals: ~70 m land surface temperature at varying times of day; captures diurnal heat signatures of operating halls and cooling plumes that Landsat's fixed morning overpass misses.
update_frequency: Irregular (ISS orbit; several scenes per month per site)
scrape_hint: Use NASA AppEEARS (https://appeears.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov/) with a free Earthdata login to extract ECO_L2T_LSTE samples as CSV/GeoTIFF.

name: UN Comtrade Plus
reveals: Monthly/annual bilateral trade by HS code (8471 computers/servers, 8473 parts, 8542/854231 processors incl. GPUs); mirrors import surges into Malaysia, Singapore, Ireland, Netherlands and Gulf states that precede compute build-outs, and export flows of used equipment.
scrape_hint: Free Basic key: 500 calls/day, 100k records/call; pip install comtradeapicall; getFinalData(key, typeCode='C', freqCode='M', cmdCode='854231,8471', ...). Public preview without key: 500 records.

name: USA Trade Online
reveals: Monthly US imports/exports at 10-digit HTS by customs district and port; isolates GPU/server (8471.50, 8473.30, 8542.31) inflows through specific ports (e.g., Anchorage, Chicago, LAX air cargo) and used-electronics exports.
scrape_hint: Free account (formerly paid); build report then export CSV; alternatively the Census International Trade API https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/intltrade/imports/hs with free key.

name: Eurostat Easy Comext (EU international trade)
reveals: Monthly EU trade by CN8 commodity and partner (DS-059322 etc.), by mode of transport; tracks server/GPU imports into Ireland, Netherlands, Germany, Nordics and intra-EU movements of used IT equipment relevant to WEEE leakage.
scrape_hint: Build query in Easy Comext (no login needed for standard datasets) and export CSV; bulk files at https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/files?file=comext/COMEXT_DATA/PRODUCTS/ .

name: ImportYeti (US bill-of-lading search)
reveals: 713 million+ customs shipment records searchable by importer or supplier; reveals which contractors/OEMs (e.g., Supermicro, Foxconn, Quanta) ship server racks to which US consignees and ports, and generator/transformer imports by data-center builders.
scrape_hint: Free sign-up gives company pages with shipment counts, suppliers and HS codes; paid tiers add exports/CSV; scrape company pages politely or use the alternative bulk CBP AMS data via FOIA.

name: Panjiva (S&P Global) global shipment data
country_or_scope: Global (US, LatAm, India, parts of Asia bill-of-lading)
reveals: Paid shipment-level database with consignee/shipper matching across many countries; the most complete source for tracing server/GPU logistics but outside a free ledger budget. Listed for completeness; not verified this session.
scrape_hint: Subscription required; use ImportYeti and national customs portals as free substitutes.

name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026
publisher: U.S. Geological Survey National Minerals Information Center
country_or_scope: Global production / US supply by commodity
reveals: Annual production, reserves, import reliance and prices for 90+ commodities (copper, gallium, germanium, tantalum, cobalt, rare earths, helium) that underpin GPUs, transformers and cooling; data release available by DOI for scripted use.
scrape_hint: Download the 2026 data release (CSV/XLSX) via the DOI link; PDF commodity sheets parse with pdfplumber.

name: Responsible Minerals Initiative public facility lists
country_or_scope: Global (3TG, cobalt, mica, copper, nickel smelters/refiners)
reveals: Public list of RMAP-conformant/active smelters and refiners by metal and country; cross-reference with SEC Form SD conflict-minerals filings of GPU/server OEMs to map upstream facilities.
scrape_hint: Use 'RMI Public List' and 'Export - Smelter Reference Lists' (XLSX) without login; full database requires membership.

name: COCHILCO copper statistics (production, energy and water in mining)
reveals: Copper/molybdenum production, mining electricity consumption (up 27.3% in a decade per Oct-2026 release) and water use (seawater vs continental); links copper demand for transformers and cabling to physical water and energy footprints.
update_frequency: Monthly bulletin; annual yearbook and water/energy reports
scrape_hint: Base de Datos Electrónica (BDE) exports XLSX; annual 'Consumo de agua' and 'Consumo de energía' reports are PDFs under Estudios.

name: Global E-waste Monitor 2024
reveals: Country estimates of e-waste generated, formally collected and documented recycling (2022 data; 62 Mt generated, 22% documented); baseline for the gap between server-grade WEEE generated and what national Basel/WEEE reports account for.
scrape_hint: Download report PDF and country-data annex from the 2024 page; UNITAR's globalewaste.org offers the statistics tables as XLSX.

name: Basel Convention National Reporting (Article 13 reports and dashboard)
reveals: Annual Party reports of hazardous-waste exports/imports by category, destination, transit and disposal method; comparing declared e-waste exports with Comtrade HS 8471/8473 'used' flows and importer records exposes undeclared e-waste movements (the Basel-vs-trade gap).
update_frequency: Annual (reports due end of following year; many Parties late)
scrape_hint: Reports listed per year under National Reports (PDF/online forms); the Electronic Reporting System (ers.basel.int) exposes tables per country-year; scrape the year index pages and download.

name: Eurostat waste statistics - WEEE (env_waselee and related)
reveals: WEEE put on market, collected, treated, recovered and exported by category (incl. 'IT and telecommunications equipment') per member state; the only harmonised official series for European server/IT equipment end-of-life.
scrape_hint: GET https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/env_waselee?format=JSON&lang=EN (JSON-stat); dataset code could not be re-confirmed this session due to fetch limits.

name: Basel Action Network e-Trash Transparency Project reports
country_or_scope: Global (US, EU, Canada, Australia tracker studies)
reveals: GPS-tracker studies that followed discarded electronics from recyclers to export destinations, naming companies and ports; independent evidence of e-waste leakage that national Basel reports omit.
scrape_hint: Server redirects https to http for this path; download report PDFs and tracker datasets (KML) linked on the page.

name: SEC EDGAR Full-Text Search
reveals: Full text of 10-K/10-Q/8-K since 2001: capex guidance, PPA and nuclear/gas supply agreements, Form SD conflict-minerals reports, and utility 10-Ks disclosing data-center load (Dominion, Entergy, AEP). Legally bound statements usable as evidence.
scrape_hint: GET https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22data%20center%22%20%22power%20purchase%22&forms=8-K with a descriptive User-Agent (name/email); <=10 req/s; returns JSON hits with filing URLs.

name: Companies House - Find and update company information
reveals: Free filing history, accounts and officers for UK data-centre SPVs and operators; charges (mortgages) registered against sites reveal financing and asset values, and accounts disclose energy costs and fixed-asset additions.
scrape_hint: REST API at https://api.company-information.service.gov.uk/ with free key (developer.company-information.service.gov.uk); accounts PDFs via /company/{number}/filing-history; bulk free products available.

name: CourtListener / RECAP Archive (Free Law Project)
reveals: Free mirror of PACER dockets and documents (RECAP), opinions and a REST API; litigation over data-center zoning, noise, water, FERC co-location and generator permits exposes site details, MW and contracts under oath.
scrape_hint: GET https://www.courtlistener.com/api/rest/v4/search/?q=%22data%20center%22&type=r with free token; bulk CSV dumps monthly; main site blocks crawlers via robots.txt so use the API.

name: MuckRock public records archive and request service
reveals: Hundreds of thousands of pages of released records searchable by agency and keyword, plus a $20/5-request filing service; prior requests on data-center tax abatements, utility contracts and permits are reusable, and new FOIAs to utilities/counties can be templated.
scrape_hint: REST API: https://www.muckrock.com/api_v1/foia/?q=data+center (token optional); documents hosted on DocumentCloud with its own API.

name: Segundo Tribunal Ambiental case management system
reveals: Electronic case files, hearings and judgments on environmental permit challenges (e.g., Google Cerrillos data-center water case), with expert reports quantifying groundwater draw; daily status and admissions listed.
scrape_hint: Expediente search at causas.tribunalambiental.cl/causas/consultas by Rol (R-/D-) or keyword; judgments under 'Sentencias' as PDFs.

name: Stockholm Exergi heat recovery (Open District Heating)
reveals: Program buying waste heat from data centers at ~2 MSEK/yr per MW; page gives aggregate '11,000 apartments heated by surplus heat' but no per-site MW; site-level figures appear in annual/sustainability reports and Stockholm Data Parks material. opendistrictheating.com now redirects here.
scrape_hint: Scrape annual and sustainability report PDFs for 'återvunnen värme' GWh; cross-check with Energimyndigheten district-heating statistics.

name: Carbon free energy for Google Cloud regions (hourly CFE% table)
reveals: Per-region hourly-matched CFE% and grid carbon intensity for 2025 (e.g., Stockholm 100%, Doha 0%), with Electricity Maps data under an SGS ISO 14064 assurance letter; machine-readable copies on GitHub and BigQuery allow independent recomputation against ENTSO-E/EIA hourly data.
scrape_hint: git clone https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/region-carbon-info (CSV per year); or BigQuery public dataset 'regional-cfe'.

name: EnergyTag Granular Certificate standard and accredited registries
reveals: Open-source hourly electricity certificate standard and list of accredited registries; the site publishes no volumes, but accredited registries are where hyperscaler hourly-CFE claims can in principle be audited.
scrape_hint: Scrape the Accredited Organizations page for registry names, then query each registry's public issuance reports.

name: Climate TRACE asset-level emissions (power sector package)
reveals: Independent, satellite- and sensor-derived emissions estimates for individual power plants, with name, coordinates, owner, capacity, MWh activity and emissions, updated monthly. Lets a gas plant attached to datacenter load be checked against an estimate the operator does not control. Does not cover datacenters as a facility type and does not attribute plant emissions to consumers.
scrape_hint: Download the power sector ZIP from climatetrace.org/downloads; open the electricity-generation asset emissions CSV; match on plant name or nearest coordinates to ledger entries; the ownership CSV gives operator and parent. API at api.climatetrace.org/v7 is beta. Also mirrored in BigQuery (trace-data-383422.climate_trace) and Zenodo.
